answer.why_different: The generated document uses different response-description values for 200, 201, 204, and default; it also changes the default response schema reference from an error schema to Resource and adds explicit 4XX/5XX response entries. These are primarily value changes, with additional response entries representing a structural expansion of the response map.
answer.spec_3gpp: The PUT operation returns a Resource representation for successful output and defines an error response as ErrorResponse. The generated default response instead describes and returns a Resource, which contradicts the error-response mapping. The detailed official distinctions for 200, 201, and 204 are also partially lost in the generated descriptions.
answer.openapi: OpenAPI requires a Responses Object and permits a default response for undeclared status codes. It also explicitly permits uppercase wildcard response ranges such as 4XX and 5XX, so the added ranges are valid response-map entries and can document client and server error responses more specifically.
answer.clearer_why: The official descriptions preserve the conditions distinguishing replacement, creation, identical updates, and no-content responses, and clearly identify the default response as an error. The generated default description incorrectly presents a Resource success response, making the response behavior misleading despite its shorter wording.

This loses response semantics; the PUT mapping confirms that status and the Resource response body are part of the operation contract (S7).
Both descriptions state that 201 means the resource was created and that its Resource representation is returned. This matches the PUT output mapping of Resource in the response body (S6, S7).

The generated description preserves identical-representation and no-body information but omits the restriction that 204 may be returned only in that case. That omission loses a condition on the status response; the PUT mapping identifies status codes as part of the operation contract (S7).

The generated default description incorrectly describes a successful createMOI Resource representation rather than an error response. The specification maps the error response body to ErrorResponse (S7, S32).

The generated default schema points to Resource instead of the ErrorResponseDefault schema, so the default error payload is replaced by a success-resource schema. The specification requires the error response to use ErrorResponse (S7), and identifies ErrorResponse as the error response-body type (S18).

The added 4XX response explicitly documents client-error responses with an ErrorResponse instead of relying only on default coverage. The specification requires status/error handling for the PUT operation (S7), and OpenAPI explicitly permits the 4XX wildcard response range (O5).

The added 5XX response explicitly documents server-error responses with an ErrorResponse instead of relying only on default coverage. OpenAPI permits the 5XX wildcard response range (O5), while the specification maps error responses for the operation (S7).

#### Responses Object  
A container for the expected responses of an operation.
The container maps a HTTP response code to the expected response.  
The documentation is not necessarily expected to cover all possible HTTP response codes because they may not be known in advance.
However, documentation is expected to cover a successful operation response and any known errors.  
The `default` MAY be used as a default response object for all HTTP codes
that are not covered individually by the specification.  
The `Responses Object` MUST contain at least one response code, and it
SHOULD be the response for a successful operation call.
